This tab answers: where do the numbers come from, and where is each view? Every number is computed in your browser from the # race data, except the official points and mountains standings, which come from published results.

This tab answers: which countries sent the most riders and teams, and whose riders did best? Riders count by nationality, teams by the country they are registered in. Click a country to list its riders and teams.

This tab answers: which riders do well on which kind of road? Terrain is the stage type: flat, hilly, mountain, or individual time trial (ITT), where riders start alone and race the clock. Pick a terrain to see who placed there and who gets faster when the road climbs.

This tab answers: which teams were strongest, and which riders carried them? The team classification adds each team's three best times on every stage. Start from the team totals, then open a team to see its riders.

This tab answers: who did best on a single day? Pick a stage on the map or in the list to see who won, by how much, their adjusted times and which teams filled the top #. Further down: all stages grouped by terrain, the time trials and the longest day.

This tab answers: who keeps finishing near the front, and who might not finish at all? Steady riders matter for questions like "will this rider finish in the top #?", not only "will they win?". You can also see who faded in week # and who left the race.

This tab answers: who won the race overall, and on which days was it decided? The yellow jersey goes to the rider with the lowest total time. Pick a rider in the standings to see the day they gained or lost the most time on the top ten, then replay the race without time bonuses or penalties.
